newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures ended weaker in thin volume on Friday but held well above near-term support despite a soft U.S. bond market.
There was very little of any consequence to give the market trading direction and the notionnel was stuck in a range between 130.30 and 130.50 for the whole of the quiet session.
The notionnel failed to react to the June IFO business climate index which printed at 96.0 compared to a May reading of 95.4.
The market was also mostly unmoved by U.S. trade data.
Comments from German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on the dollar and France's EMU position were equally unimpressive to the market.
"We should leave the French to do what they themselves want to do. It is not for me to say," Kohl told a news conference when asked how he rated the country's chances of joining EMU.

Futures were supported by continued high liquidity and a feeling among investors that the Socialist-led government would do what it had to to plug the deficit hole to qualify for European monetary union.
The outlook for the U.S. economy, with continued growth and low inflation on the horizon, was also a supporting factor.
The socialists were seen pushing hard to cut the deficit, and for debt market investors reaching the target -- or getting near to it -- was more important than how they got there.

The government will receive the results of an independent audit of public finances at 0700 GMT on Monday and later the same day will announce measures to curb the deficit, which government sources have said is likely to be about 3.6 percent of GDP.
The audit will be made public at 0830 GMT on Monday.

The measures being studied to narrow the gap include a rise in corporate tax, an increase in company social security contributions, a rise in savings taxes targetting the well off and a review of income tax cuts promised by the previous government, a source close to the government said on Thursday.
Spending cuts were also being considered, the source said.
PIBOR was being supported by Euromarks, which were trading on hopes of rate increases in Europe that analysts have described as "irrational".
